entries.detail: Rule applies only to {tsx,jsx,ts,js,html,vue,svelte}; the only in-scope target is panel.html (the akin .swift files and REDESIGN_SPECS.md are out of scope for this rule, not audited). Read panel.html's savePrompt handler (lines 1827-1847), wired to the Save button (id="save", line 668) via `$('save').addEventListener('click', savePrompt);` at line 1973. Inside savePrompt, the fetch call `const r = await fetch('/api/queued', {...})` at lines 1834-1837 has no pending-state handling at all: the Save button is never set to `.disabled = true` and no `` (the pattern used correctly elsewhere in this same file, e.g. runFix at lines 1924-1926 and 1953, and the reopen handler at lines 2007-2019) is shown while the POST is in flight. A user who double-clicks Save during a slow request can fire duplicate `/api/queued` POSTs, and there is no animated indicator during the wait, violating both halves of the rule (no pending state driving a spinner during the request). Contrast this with runFix, which correctly disables the button and swaps in ` working` before its fetch and restores state in a `finally` block; savePrompt has no such treatment. Fix: in savePrompt, disable `$('save')` and swap its content for ` Saving` immediately before the fetch, and restore it (enabled, original label) in a try/finally regardless of success or failure.

Ran `rg -n 'beforeunload|useBeforeUnload|onRouteChangeStart'` and a broader `grep -n -i 'beforeunload|visibilitychange|pagehide'` over panel.html: zero matches in the whole 2563-line file. The queue textarea `<textarea id="box" placeholder="What do you want to hand off next?" aria-describedby="box-why box-err"></textarea>` (line 665) holds local dirty state: its own helper text at line 660 says 'Ϙ⏎ saves' and it is gated behind an explicit `<button ... id="save">Save</button>` (line 667), with only an `input` listener at line 1978 that clears an error message, not a save. Fix: add `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', e => { if ($('box').value.trim() !== lastSavedValue) { e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; } })` (or equivalent dirty-check) so the browser warns before the tab/page is closed or navigated away with unsaved queue text. I did not flag the to-do checkboxes (line 1679) since their `change` handler (line 1754) fires an immediate `fetch('/api/todos/toggle', ...)` (line 1763), so there is no unsaved local state there. entries.detail:
Read panel.html end to end for state-changing calls (grep for setUrlParam/setView/searchParams). The page has a "Different rung" tab control (cards, book, queue, to-do — button at line 691, handler `b.addEventListener('click', () => setView(b.dataset.view));` at line 1967) whose active view lives only in the `currentView` module variable and a `.active` class toggle (setView, defined line 717-731). setUrlParam (line 710-715) exists and IS used, but only for the `asin` param (line 1240) and is never called from setView. On load, the view is hardcoded to `setView('flashcards')` (line 2558) rather than reading any URL param, and no code anywhere reads a `view`/`tab` query param. So refreshing the page or sharing the panel.html link always drops the user back on the flashcards rung, losing which of the four tabs (cards/book/queue/todo) they were on. Fix: mirror the current rung into the URL inside setView (e.g. `setUrlParam('view', name)` guarded against re-triggering on fromServer) and read it back on load (`new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('view') || 'flashcards'`) before calling setView, the same pattern already used for `asin`.

Scope note: the rule's applies_to (tsx/jsx/ts/js/html/vue/svelte) covers panel.html but not the five akin *.swift files or REDESIGN_SPECS.md audited alongside it — those are a native SwiftUI app with no URL/query-param concept, so the rule does not apply to them; I did not flag anything there. I did not need to consult the goal-loop notes file since this rule's subject is the codebase, not the session.</detail>

The rule targets web frontend code using router frameworks (React Router, Vue Router, etc.) to detect router.push/navigate calls on non-anchor elements. Rule scope (**/*.{tsx,jsx,ts,js,html,vue,svelte}) only matches panel.html among the targets; the Swift files and REDESIGN_SPECS.md are not_applicable to this rule and were not audited against it. In panel.html I grepped for modal/dialog/overlay state and for URL-sync usage (location.hash, pushState, replaceState, URLSearchParams), then read the two overlay-open functions. The app has working deep-link infrastructure: `setUrlParam(key,value)` (line 710) calls `history.replaceState`, and it IS used for one piece of state, the selected book: `setUrlParam('asin', asin)` at line 1240, read back via `new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('asin')` at line 1647. But the two role="dialog" aria-modal="true" overlays defined at lines 635 and 642 (#reader-menu-overlay, #star-cal-overlay) are opened purely by class toggling with no URL write: `ov.classList.add('open');` at panel.html:2213 inside `openReaderMenu()` (line 2205), and `document.getElementById('star-cal-overlay').classList.add('open');` at panel.html:2349 inside `_openStarCal()` (line 2348). Neither open path calls setUrlParam or touches location.hash, so a user cannot copy a link that lands directly in the reading menu or the star calendar (nor can it survive a refresh) even though the codebase already has the exact utility (setUrlParam) to do it for the asin param. Fix: call `setUrlParam('menu','1')` / `setUrlParam('cal', yyyyMM or day)` on open and clear the param on close (closeReaderMenu line 2219, _closeStarCal line 2358), and on load check those params to re-open the overlay, mirroring how the asin param already restores view state.

entries.detail: Searched all targets for <select> elements. panel.html contains no select elements. Swift files are iOS native code, not HTML. REDESIGN_SPECS.md is documentation. The rule applies only to HTML select form controls; zero such elements exist in any target file.

Computed WCAG contrast ratios (relative-luminance formula) for every --fg/--bg token pair declared in the shared token block (lines 16-46), across both the light :root (16-36) and the dark @media(prefers-color-scheme:dark) override (38-46): --muted, --faint, --ink, --edge, --ok/--warn/--crit against --ground/--raised all clear 4.5:1 (text) or 3:1 (UI) in both themes, and --on-accent on --accent (button.act.primary, line 361) is 7.06:1 light / 6.98:1 dark. However `button.act small { ... opacity: .7 ... }` at line 364 sets a 9px sub-label (e.g. the ease-rating digit in `<button class="act primary" data-ease="3">Good<small>3</small></button>` at line 545, an enabled, non-disabled interactive control) to 70% opacity on top of --on-accent/--accent. Blending --on-accent at alpha .7 over --accent yields only 4.23:1 in the light theme and 4.15:1 in the dark theme, both below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal-size text (9px does not qualify as 'large text' under WCAG, which needs >=18.66px bold or >=24px regular). This is exactly the class of miss the rule calls out: a token-pair audit of body text passes, but the opacity-modified small label on an active (not disabled) primary button fails AA in both theme flips. Disabled-state opacities (button.act[disabled] opacity .45 at line 365, and #companions button.do[disabled] opacity .5 at line 129) were also computed (~2.5-3.8:1) but are WCAG-exempt as inactive UI components, so not reported as offenses. In panel.html I ran `grep -n -i "hover\|:focus\|:active\|opacity"` and read every match (lines 86, 114, 129, 179, 191-195, 324, 329, 361-365, 420, 433, 440, 451, 1691) plus the :root token block (lines 16-45). Every interactive-state rule increases prominence relative to rest: `.rungs button:focus-visible`, `.cal-star:focus-visible`, `button.act:focus-visible`, `ul.todo button.pick:focus-visible`, `button.linkish:focus-visible`, and `textarea:focus` all add a 2px solid var(--accent) outline (line 86, 329, 362, 433, 440, 451) where none exists at rest. `#companions .top button:hover` and `button.act:hover` change border-color to var(--accent), a higher-contrast accent color, from an unstyled/transparent resting border (lines 114, 361). `ul.todo li:hover` sets background to var(--raised), a lighter/distinct surface from the base list background (line 420), which is a state change, not a contrast reduction. `.reader-pager-overlay:hover`/`:focus-within` sets opacity from 0 to 1 (lines 191-195), i.e. hover/focus INCREASE visibility from fully transparent, the opposite of a violation. The only `opacity: .5`/`.35`/`.45`/`.7`/`.55` reductions found (lines 129, 324, 364, 365, 1691) are on `[disabled]` states, empty calendar cells, and a small subtitle label, none of which are hover/active/focus pseudo-states. Read panel.html around lines 1108-1112 (readerSay), 1264-1288 (renderReader), and the #reader-over markup at lines 559-570. entries.detail: Read panel.html end to end and traced every addEventListener('click',...) handler for its success/failure feedback path (companions-recheck, save, reader-retry-yes, signin-chrome, carry-session, runFix at line 1921, and the todo checkbox toggle all wrap their fetch in try/catch or check r.ok, and always resolve the status line to an explicit success or failure message). The 'advance' handler at lines 1989-1992 is the exception: `$('advance').addEventListener('click', async () => { say('next', true); await fetch('/api/advance', { method: 'POST' }); say(''); });`. It shows a spinner via say('next', true), then awaits fetch with no try/catch and never checks response.ok. fetch() only rejects on a network failure, not on a non-2xx status, so a server error (e.g. HTTP 500 from /api/advance) still resolves normally and say('') fires, silently clearing the spinner as if the click succeeded even though nothing actually changed. On a genuine network failure the awaited fetch throws, the uncaught rejection skips say(''), and the spinner plus 'next' text is left on screen indefinitely with no error surfaced. Either path leaves this one user click, out of every clickable control in the file, with no true success-or-failure signal. Fix: wrap the fetch in try/catch, check response.ok, and call say() with a concrete success or failure message on both paths, matching the pattern already used by savePrompt (line 1827-1844) and runFix (lines 1921-1953). The akin Swift views (QuestionnaireBrowseView, QuestionnaireDetailView, SubscriptionsView, ProfileSwitcherView, AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel) and REDESIGN_SPECS.md were not in scope for this finding: the rule's applies_to list (tsx/jsx/ts/js/html/vue/svelte) does not include .swift, and no runtime app was available to drive interactively (this was a static-code trace, not a Playwright session against a live server), so Swift button/action feedback could not be behaviorally verified and is not claimed as pass or fail here.
entries.rule_title: Every user-initiated action produces a visible signal within seconds
